summary_paragraph: A 34-year-old woman was admitted with fevers and toe pain, initially treated for cellulitis. Blood cultures revealed MSSA bacteremia, likely originating from her left chest port. She was started on IV vancomycin, and the port was surgically removed. After confirming source control and no endocarditis on echocardiogram, she was transitioned to IV nafcillin. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. Her infection resolved, and she was discharged to an extended care facility to complete a two-week course of antibiotics. Diarrhea developed during treatment but was C. diff-negative and managed supportively. Her bipolar disorder, chronic pain, and other comorbidities were maintained on prior regimens without complication.
problems: Local infection due to central venous catheter, initial encounter
Sepsis due to Methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus
